Stage B1 (batched left-padded vs unbatched last-token margins, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) FAILS the plan's 1e-2 bound in bf16: max |diff| = 0.284, mean = 0.039 logits. The same check in fp32 gives max 9.5e-06 (mean 3.8e-06), so padding/positions are exact and the gap is bf16 kernel rounding that depends on batch shape. Every candidate compares passes with the SAME batch composition (skip-pass reference reproduces the base pass bit-exactly: max diff 0.0), so this per-item noise (~0.04 logits) enters candidates only through perturbation-dependent rounding; it is below the 0.25-logit variance floor and informative-pair threshold. [v2 note: this claim was false for C9 in v1, where true-patching and AtP numerators/denominators mixed 8-row and 16-row passes. v2 fixes it (CODE_FIXES_POST_REVIEW_V2 item 4).] Session 4 (GPU, CUDA bf16): on the same check, max |diff| = 0.498 and mean = 0.139 logits (scratch/stage_b_cuda_Qwen__Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.json). The GPU bf16 kernels depend on batch shape more than the CPU ones. The same-batch-composition design is what keeps this out of the candidates. B2, B3, B5 and D pass on the GPU row; B4 (C2 0.127 vs its null p95 0.324) is recorded as measured. anisotropy-matched random directions v = A^T g almost never fall within +/-25% of var(Ah): on the smoke model 0/2000 draws were accepted at every B_mid layer (closest ratios 2.0-3.9), so the pre-registered 'closest by |ratio-1|' fallback is used; per-model acceptance counts and picked ratios are in rows/*.json random_dirs GPU rows (session 4): 63 of 216 (model, candidate, B_mid layer) cells had at least one accepted draw in 2000 tries; the picked directions' activation-variance ratio var(Av)/var(Ah) has median 2.89 (5-95%: 0.90-8.70). The random directions typically carry several times the harm direction's variance. That is expected to widen the direction-null p95 used by S2(b); it was not tested with an exactly variance-matched null (see RESULTS 4c for the S2(b) decomposition).
the iter-2 F2b_rosi__4 graded cell used 64 harmful + 32 benign twins (verified by exact item-id match), not the 64+64 stated in the plan; the 128-token arm uses the same 96 items

The pod restarted at ~16:48 UTC and killed the session-1 panel loop during model 10/21. Session 2 (17:05 UTC) resumed from the persisted rows. No sibling agents were running in the container after the restart, so timings after 17:05 are uncontended. A second pod restart at ~17:37 UTC killed the session-2 v2 driver (run_panel_v2.sh) after 4 of 19 v2 sub-panel rows. Session 3 (17:53 UTC) resumed from the persisted rows with run_panel_v3.sh. The 4 rows measured on 2 threads in session 2 were moved to scratch/rows_v2_session2_2threads/ and re-measured, so every row in rows/ was measured in session 3 with the same code on the same 4-thread CPU allocation. An independent code review (session 2) found no error in any primary plain-condition value, but found 3 MAJOR and 4 MINOR issues, all fixed in method.py/live_lib.py v2: (1) the offset control's C1 ran its first perturbed call on a stale KV cache still holding the last prompt token, so m_plus was wrong; fixed by cropping the cache after the offset base pass, plus an assert in last_call. (2) In 16-layer models C3's band-5 'middle layer' was the FINAL layer, where last-token patching gives f=1 by construction; the final layer is never patched now. (3) The C9 ATP_UNRELIABLE rule was not implemented; it now lives in analyze_live.py, and true patching is also run under both wrapped poles (true_patch_pole_*), with a k8 subset. (4) The C9 numerators mixed 8-row and 16-row bf16 batch shapes; each reference now comes from the same batch shape. (5) The C1 linearity check now uses item-level absolute one-sided differences and is 'undetermined' below 0.05 logits. (6) C3_sharp is now max_b(f_b - f_{b-1}) for b>=1, and C3_depth is the depth of the patched layer. (7) The C1/C2 oracle rows now need >=2 judged items per class, the same gate as C16_oracle; C16_oracle's direction is in-sample (stated in each row). EVERY row was re-measured with v2 code. The v1 rows and code are kept in scratch/rows_v1_pre_review/ and scratch/code_v1_pre_review/ for provenance. PREREG.json is unchanged (same hash).

The plan's constant-offset control set is Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, TinyLlama, OLMo-2-1B and SmolLM2-360M. Session 1 substituted Qwen3-0.6B for Qwen3-4B (outside the CPU sub-panel). The GPU rows run the plan's set plus Qwen3-0.6B, so the control covers 7 models: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen/Qwen3-4B, TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct, unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. The C9 AtP-validation set keeps its session-1 substitute (Qwen2.5-0.5B for Qwen3-4B). C9 true patching is measured on every model, so the per-model AtP-vs-true Pearson is reported for all.

Session 4 ran on a new pod with an NVIDIA L4 (23 GB; cgroup 15.3 CPUs / 71 GB RAM), after the third pod restart. It built the CUDA venv venv_gpu (torch 2.14.0 CUDA build, transformers 4.57.6; same versions as venv_live apart from the CUDA build). It made method.py/live_lib.py device-agnostic with device plumbing only: model and batch on the device, .cpu() before numpy, hook vectors on the hidden state's device, torch.cuda.synchronize() in the per-block timers, set_per_process_memory_fraction(9.3/total), no RLIMIT_AS under CUDA, and a GRAD_CHUNKED halving fallback for the backward pass. Candidate definitions, directions, folds, seeds, bands, prompts and judge calls are unchanged. Measured on the GPU: 36 rows (23 graded), in full mode with the PREREG time caps. PREREG's pre-declared GPU-branch constants apply: [20] anisotropy-matched random directions (PREREG n_gpu = 20; its 'used': 8 and compute_mode.cuda = false describe the CPU state when the file was hashed at 15:59:59Z, and the file is unchanged), and all 5 C16 alphas in every variant, because the 3-alpha variant grid was a CPU-only budget cut. VRAM peak: max 10.52 GB over 36 rows (cap 9.3 GB). The backward pass fell back to chunks on: ['DreamFast/qwen3-4b-heretic', 'HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B', 'Qwen/Qwen3-4B', 'Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base', 'Qwen/Qwen3-4B-SafeRL', 'lunahr/Phi-4-mini-instruct-abliterated', 'microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct', 'mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated']. Rows not measured on CUDA: none. S5 (<120 s per 4B model on the GPU, excluding load) is measurable in this session. The 12 CPU rows of session 3 (12 files in scratch/rows_cpu_v3/) are compared with their GPU re-measurement in candidates_live.json 'cross_hardware'. That comparison is descriptive only. torch 2.14 routes the RoPE outer product (inv_freq @ position_ids) through a Triton 'native DSL' kernel that JIT-compiles a C helper; this pod has no libc headers, so every model failed to load until TORCH_DISABLE_NATIVE_JIT=1 was set (method.py sets it before importing torch). torch then uses its standard ATen kernels, so no measured quantity depends on this switch.

2 ungraded chat models ran out of memory under the plan's 9.3 GB VRAM cap in run_panel_gpu.sh, even with the 1-item backward fallback: Llama-3.2-3B-abliterated (3.6 B, untied embeddings) in the backward pass, and Phi-3.5-mini (3.8 B, 32 KV heads) in the first base pass. The plan's fallback 2 prescribes halving the batch to 8 and then 4. Instead they were re-run (run_panel_gpu_retry.sh) with the cap raised to [12.0] GB, which is still inside a 16 GB worker. That keeps their 16-item batches, and therefore the bf16 numerics, identical to every other model's. Each of these rows carries a VRAM_CAP_RAISED flag. Both models are ungraded and enter no correlation. They do enter the S5 (~4B timing) set.

Robust-Decoding/gemma2-2b-it-hh-dpo-harmless-step-6000 ships no tokenizer files. The repo holds only the config, weights and an empty auto-generated card; vocab_size is 256000, the Gemma-2 vocabulary. It failed to load (RUN_FAIL) in run_panel_gpu.sh. It was re-run in run_panel_gpu_retry.sh with the tokenizer and chat template of its panel lineage root, unsloth/gemma-2-2b-it (live_lib.TOKENIZER_FROM_LINEAGE). This borrows the family tokenizer, not any parent weights or activations, so the model is still read alone. The row is ungraded and carries a TOKENIZER_FROM_LINEAGE flag.
